title: Collaboration through digital technologies
competency: Explain digital collaboration, its three components and the main kinds of collaborative tools, and use them in a group task.

keywords.def: Working with other individuals or teams and getting things done using digital devices and technology.
Software and apps that help people work together: communication, file sharing, project management, data visualization and notetaking tools.

ideas.name: Digital collaboration and its three components

en.text: Digital collaboration means working with other people or teams and getting things done with digital devices and technology. It improves communication, document and content management and information flow, so people are more productive. The Internet lets people collaborate in real time across time zones and distance. Its three components are people, who need agreed workflows; collaborative tools, chosen for features, price, usage policies and ease of use; and devices such as smartphones, tablets and laptops.

screens.title: Digital collaboration
paras: Working with other people or teams using digital devices and technology.
It can include tools, apps, software, procedures and processes.
It improves communication, document and content management, and information flow.
It matters to organisations, schools, communities and creative groups.
The Internet allows real-time work across time zones and distance (Figure 1.20).

screens.title: Three components
paras: They need workflows and practices to stay in touch, even remotely (e.g. during COVID-19).
Collaborative tools: choose by features, price, usage policies and ease of use.
How well people use the tool decides how well it works.
Devices: smartphones, tablets and laptops are the physical media we connect with.

software chosen for features, price, policies and ease of use

en.text: The book names five kinds of collaborative tools. Communication tools (Microsoft Teams, Zoom, Google Meet, Skype, Webex, Slack, Yammer) offer messaging, conference calls and video chat with screen sharing. Documentation and file-sharing tools (Google Drive, Google Docs, Dropbox, SharePoint, MediaFire) offer comments, track changes, versions and access control. Project management tools (Trello, Asana, ClickUp) manage tasks; data visualization tools (Tableau, Power BI, Google Charts) show data; notetaking tools (Evernote, OneNote, Google Keep) capture notes.

screens.title: Activity 1.8: a group collaboration task
steps: Write a half-page summary in a new cloud document named "Digital Collaboration Activity – your group name".
Share the document link with all members by email or social media.
Choose a screen-sharing meeting tool (Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams).
One member creates the meeting link; others join, share the screen and edit the document live.
Discuss how the tools improve learning and teamwork; share with the class.

screens.title: Key word
defs: Software and apps that help people work together: communication, file sharing, project management, data visualization and notetaking tools.

screens.title: Sort the tools
screens.why: The book groups each tool by its main purpose (p.20).
screens.clue: Ask what the tool mainly does: talk, store, plan, chart or note.

screens.text: Which feature belongs to documentation and file-sharing tools?
Your class uses a Telegram group to share announcements and questions. Which kind of tool is it?
screens.clue: What do members do in the group?

screens.title: Order the steps of Activity 1.8
items: Write the summary in a cloud document
Meet, share the screen and co-edit
Discuss and share with the class
screens.why: Create, share, choose a tool, meet and edit, reflect.
screens.clue: You cannot share a link before the document exists.

screens.text: In Activity 1.8 your group must co-edit a summary while discussing it live. Which pair of tool kinds do you need?
opts: Documentation and file sharing, plus communication with screen sharing
screens.ans: Documentation and file sharing, plus communication with screen sharing
screens.why: A cloud document for co-editing, and a meeting tool to talk and share the screen.
screens.clue: One tool for the document, one for the talk.
